walls.title: Retaining wall
walls.description: Sliding, overturning and bearing checks for cantilever and gravity walls.
walls.type_picker.title: Retaining wall type
walls.type.cantilever.description: Reinforced concrete cantilever wall with a stem and base slab.
walls.type.gravity.description: Mass concrete or masonry wall resisting earth pressure by its own weight.
walls.placeholder: This section's screens will be moved into this module in a later step.
walls.type_picker.subtitle: Choose the type of retaining wall to design.
walls.type_picker.load_error: Wall types could not be loaded.
walls.type_picker.name: Wall name
walls.type_picker.empty_desc: There are no retaining wall types to choose from.
walls.soil_source.title: Soil source
walls.soil_source.no_profile: The project has no soil profile; enter the wall soil manually.
walls.soil_source.manual_hint: This soil belongs to this wall only. You must enter the unit weights and the groundwater depth yourself.
walls.soil_source.gwt_hint: A large depth (below the profile bottom) means there is no groundwater.
walls.options.title: Analysis options
walls.options.kv.title: Vertical seismic coefficient (kv) sign
walls.options.kv.hint: TBDY 16.12.2.3. kv is positive upward: the thrust uses (1−kv) and the vertical wall inertia is +kv·W.
walls.options.kv.envelope.desc: Each check is evaluated for +|kv| and −|kv| and the unfavourable one is kept. The result cards show the governing sign.
walls.options.submerged.title: Seismic thrust in submerged backfill
walls.options.submerged.hint: TBDY Eq. 16.26 and the dynamic water thrust of Eq. 16.20. It only applies when the groundwater in the backfill is above the wall base level.
walls.options.submerged.envelope.desc: Both the impervious and the pervious case are computed; the one that maximises the soil increment plus the dynamic water thrust is used.
walls.options.submerged.impervious.desc: All submerged backfill layers are treated as impervious (γsat based).
walls.options.submerged.pervious.desc: All submerged layers are treated as pervious (γ based); the dynamic water thrust is added.
Each layer is classified by the engine from its entered k; layers without k are reported in the result warnings.
walls.options.submerged.missing_k: k is needed for the “By permeability” option. Retained-side layers without k: {ids}. The result warnings show which layers the calculation actually used and how they were classified.
walls.options.submerged.all_k: All retained-side layers have k entered.
walls.options.submerged.go_soil: Enter k in the Soil step
walls.options.uplift.title: Base uplift
walls.options.uplift.hint: Decides on which side the moment of the water pressure under the base is counted.
walls.options.uplift.resisting.desc: The uplift moment is deducted from the resisting moment.
walls.options.gwt_bearing.title: Bearing capacity
walls.options.gwt_bearing.label: Groundwater correction
walls.options.gwt_bearing.desc: When the groundwater lies within B below the base, the unit weight in the drained N_γ term is interpolated.
walls.options.passive.title: Passive resistance (sliding)
walls.options.passive.hint: The Rankine passive resistance of the soil in front of the toe is used for sliding only.
walls.options.passive.basic_note: Passive resistance is not used at the basic level (ASD, default settings). Select the advanced level to use it.
walls.options.passive.desc: Fraction of the Rankine passive resistance that is used, (0–1]. There is no verified normative source for the default 0.5; the value is an engineering choice and is recorded as such in the calculation notes.
walls.options.passive.unconfirmed: The reduction {value} is not confirmed yet. The program default is not a code value; Suggest / Check cannot run until it is confirmed.
walls.options.passive.confirmed: The reduction {value} is confirmed as an engineering choice.
walls.options.passive.confirm: I confirm {value} as my engineering choice
walls.options.passive.code_note: The design code's own passive participation factor (e.g. TBDY 0.3) is applied in addition to this reduction.
walls.perm.title: Soil permeability (k)
walls.perm.hint: The hydraulic conductivity k [m/s] is needed for the “By permeability” option of the Loads/seismic step. Use scientific notation (e.g. 1e-5); an empty cell means “k not entered”. The calculation engine does the classification and reports warnings in the result.
walls.result.kv_governing_hint: Vertical seismic coefficient sign governing this check in the envelope
walls.result.kv_envelope_note: kv sign (TBDY 16.12.2.3): with the envelope each check is evaluated for +|kv| (up) and −|kv| (down) and the unfavourable one is kept; the badge on a card shows the kv sign that governed that check.
walls.governing.sizing_line: Sizing-governing check (last one that forced a wider base): {label}
walls.governing.minimum_width_line: The proposal is the smallest allowed base width; no check set the width.
walls.perm.invalid_cleared: Invalid entry cleared; k counts as not entered for this layer. Enter a number k > 0 (e.g. 1e-5).
walls.run.passive_unconfirmed: Passive resistance is on and the reduction {value} is not confirmed in this session. The calculation notes record it as an “engineering choice”; confirm it in the Loads/seismic step.
walls.result.stale_inputs: The inputs changed after this result; the result shown is out of date. Recalculate.
walls.result.stale_job: The last calculation did not complete (failed, cancelled or still running); the result shown belongs to an earlier run.
walls.result.section_geometry_only: The section shows the result geometry only; the result does not carry the soil layers or the backfill slope used in the calculation.
walls.loads.surcharge_basis_horizontal: Horizontal projection (vertical q per horizontal area)
walls.loads.surcharge_basis_inclined: Inclined surface (q / cos β on the horizontal)
walls.loads.sds_range: S_DS must be greater than 0 and less than 3.
walls.loads.r_range: r must be greater than 0 and at most 2.
walls.run.seismic_invalid: A seismic input is out of range; correct or clear it in the Loads/seismic step.
walls.warning.shear_key_bearing: Key depth is not added to the bearing embedment (deliberate conservative assumption: bearing capacity is under-estimated)
walls.warning.shear_key_water: Groundwater is above the key tip ({depth} m): the extra hydrostatic uplift on the key bottom and the water thrusts on the key-tip plane are included; pressures are taken as hydrostatic, seepage around the key (flow net) is not computed
walls.warning.shear_key_reduces_sliding: The plane through the key tip gives lower sliding safety than the key-less base surface (the sliding safety is the smaller of the two surfaces); check the soil strength below the key and the base friction assumption
walls.key.enable_hint: A concrete key under the base slab along the full length; the passive resistance in front adds to sliding resistance.
walls.key.width_too_large: Key width cannot exceed the base width
walls.key.note: Key depth is not added to the bearing embedment (conservative); no reinforced-concrete design of the key, only V and M demands.
walls.key.result_note: The with-key factor is the smaller of the two candidate surfaces; the key can reduce sliding safety, in which case a warning is shown.
walls.at_rest.title: At-rest (K0) lateral earth pressure
walls.at_rest.subtitle: Along a vertical wall: σ′h = K0·(σ′v + q) plus hydrostatic water pressure; K0 is each layer's approved design value (Das).
walls.at_rest.no_profiles: The project has no soil profile. Create one in the Soil module first.
